title.narrative: Improved Nutrition Outcomes through Integrated Services for Hard-to-Reach Rural Populations in Baydhaba District (NOURISH)

description.narrative: ltpgtThis 12-month project will strengthen access to life-saving nutrition services for children with SAM in rural Baydhaba by combining quality OTP service delivery with strong MIYCN prevention and integrated protection measures. The approach will focus on bringing services closer to families, ensuring continuity of care, and addressing feeding and care practices that contribute to malnutrition. HIDIG will operate one fixed OTP sites in ADC1 supported by seven outreach service points in Bonkay, Kulmiye, Ber Shibele, Bulo Nasib, Cashi, El Edow, Munabir, Waberi, Makiney, Qasalow, and Goblanbeeri. This mixed fixed and outreach model will reduce access barriers, support regular attendance, and ensure services are delivered in safe and dignified settings. OTP service days will be coordinated with health partners operating in the same catchment areas to align referrals, routine child health services, and immunization.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtOver the project period, 3,000 children under five years of age with uncomplicated SAM (1,500g and 1,500b) will be admitted for treatment. Referrals will be generated through Family MUAC, routine CHW screening, mass MUAC and oedema screening, and referrals from stabilization centres and TSFP sites. Referrals made by CHWs will be reviewed regularly to maintain screening accuracy and prevent inappropriate admissions or exclusion of eligible cases.ltbrgtReferral pathways will be actively managed to ensure timely transfer of children with medical complications to stabilization centres and smooth transitions between SC, OTP, and TSFP services. Nutrition Officers and the Programme Manager will coordinate referrals, data sharing, and follow-up with partners to reduce defaulting and treatment interruptions. Relapse prevention will be reinforced through structured IYCF counselling, Care Group support, and 36 cooking demonstrations promoting improved household diets, hygiene practices, and appropriate use of nutrition commodities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo strengthen prevention and quality of care, the project will invest in capacity building for frontline staff and community actors. A five-day MIYCN training will be delivered to 34 health and nutrition workers serving both fixed and outreach platforms, focusing on practical IYCF counselling, maternal nutrition, growth monitoring, infant feeding in emergencies, micronutrient supplementation, and integration of MIYCN into routine services. In parallel, 24 Community Health Workers will receive a three-day IYCF training to strengthen household-level counselling, Care Group supervision, and community-based behaviour change. CHWs will support 24 Care Groups for women and men, providing sustained peer support, household outreach, family MUAC promotion, and follow-up of at-risk children and caregivers. Group IYCF education sessions will be conducted routinely at all fixed and outreach sites, reaching 1,200 caregivers, with practical demonstrations on breastfeeding, complementary feeding, responsive feeding, hygiene, and preparation of locally available nutritious foods, including the Kobciye Shurbad approach. Caregivers requiring additional support, particularly mothers of infants under six months with breastfeeding challenges, will receive targeted follow-up.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProtection principles will be applied throughout implementation to ensure assistance reaches those most at risk of exclusion. The project will target 10,829 people (4,130 women, 447 men, 3,120 girls, and 3,132 boys) across the twelve villages, using vulnerability criteria informed by IPC analysis, drought impacts, displacement pressures, and access constraints. Transparent targeting processes, clear communication of entitlements, and accessible complaints and feedback mechanisms will be established to ensure confidentiality, accountability, and protection from retaliation. Community engagement, including work with women’s and men’s groups and clear management of gatekeeper roles with zero tolerance for PSEA, will support safe and equitable service delivery.lt/pgt
